title: Classify a worker usage-limit stop as typed paused_limit
action: Per D1/D2: in run.rs, wait_for_round gains a limit classification — when the heartbeat is stale (the arm that today returns TimedOutIdle) AND the pane's recent text (pane read by recorded pane id) matches a const LIMIT_PATTERNS list (case-insensitive substrings; initially: 'hit your session limit', 'usage limit'), the poll returns a new PollDecision::PausedLimit. RunOutcome grows PausedLimit; it NEVER closes the pane (should_close_pane false even under --close-always), the JSON result carries outcome "paused_limit", the process exit stays nonzero-but-distinct, and job.json is stamped paused_limit_at (rfc3339 now) + limit_reset_hint (the raw matched pane line, trimmed). Tests: stale heartbeat + matching pane text = paused_limit with pane kept under close_always; stale heartbeat + non-matching text = timed_out_idle unchanged; fresh heartbeat + matching text = keep waiting (an active worker printing about limits is not paused).

truths: Stale heartbeat + limit-pattern pane text yields paused_limit, pane kept even under --close-always, job.json stamped
timed_out_idle behavior unchanged when no pattern matches
